newsitem.title: FRANCE: Rhone-Rorer has some Japan Taxotere go-ahead.
newsitem.headline: Rhone-Rorer has some Japan Taxotere go-ahead.

text.p: Franco-American drugs group Rhone-Poulenc Rorer said its new anti-cancer drug Taxotere had obtained market approval in Japan for breast cancer and some lung cancer treatments.
Rhone-Poulenc Rorer is majority-owned by Rhone-Poulenc.

Rorer said that Taxotere was the first product of the taxoides class to receive Japanese market authorisation. Taxoides are drugs that fight cancer cells by inhibiting their cell division, causing these cells to die.
Taxotere has already received market authorisation in more than 35 countries.
"We are pleased with the approval of Taxotere by the Japanese authorities," Gary Shearman, senior vice-president pharmaceutical development, was quoted as saying.
"The medical corps now disposes of a new anti-cancer agent to treat two of the five most common tumours in Japan," he added.
